newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish ex-minister furthers anti-Islamist bid.
newsitem.headline: Turkish ex-minister furthers anti-Islamist bid.

text.p: A former Turkish cabinet minister on Friday stepped up his campaign to forge an "Islamist-free" government to replace Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's divided coalition.

Yalim Erez, a secularist who resigned last month as trade and industry minister in protest at rising Islamist fervour, met the head of the left-wing Republican People's Party (CHP) during the afternoon, state-run Anatolian news agency said.
"We had a very beneficial talk...After this talk the end of the tunnel can be seen very clearly and openly," Erez was quoted as saying after meeting with CHP leader Deniz Baykal.
The consultations were the latest in a series of attempts by Erez, a pillar of the mainstream business community, to oust Erbakan and his Islam-based Welfare Party.
Erez has been trying to drum up support for a secularist pact since he resigned over the government's reluctance to comply with army demands for a crackdown on Islamist activism.

However, he must overcome years of mistrust among the mainstream secularist parties, whose squabbling allowed Erbakan to become modern Turkey's first Islamist leader with just 21 percent of the popular vote.

Parliament sources said Erez, of the conservative True Path Party, was expected to meet other leaders early next week and would then hold talks with True Path leader Tansu Ciller, junior partner in the Erbakan government.
On Thursday, Erez emerged from a session with main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz, of the Motherland Party, confident that he could forge a deal.

"What is important is that I have no more worries about the formation of an alternative government," Erez told reporters after talks with Yilmaz. Motherland sources said a second meeting was likely next week.
